ResearchProjectDef.label: mystic botany
ResearchProjectDef.description: Wild mystic flowers grow across the rim. Learning which ones hold mana, and how to plant them again, is where every Botania colony starts.

ResearchProjectDef.label: garden craft
ResearchProjectDef.description: Bind livingwood and livingrock into a staff that can channel mana. This is where the wand of the forest is built, and where the colony learns to shape living materials instead of only cutting them.

ResearchProjectDef.label: manasteel
ResearchProjectDef.description: Fold mana powder into steel to make manasteel: light, tough, and the skeleton of every advanced mana structure, from pools and relays to fluxfields and repairers.

ResearchProjectDef.label: mana grid
ResearchProjectDef.description:
A mana grid is the colony's reserve plus the plumbing that reaches it. A manasteel-lined pool holds 100,000 mana where a simple livingrock pool holds 2,000, and a relay tower stretches a pool's supply circle out to 11 tiles, chaining further as long as each link overlaps a group that already reaches a pool.

Everything else in the tree is priced against that grid. A generating flower has to stand inside a pool's circle (4 tiles simple, 7 manasteel) or a relay's 11, a functional flower has to reach the same reserve to pay its bill, and a turret flower has to be covered before it will fire. One pool with a ring of relays around it is what turns a scattering of flowers into an industry.

Full numbers and derivations: gameplay guide.

ResearchProjectDef.label: mana application
ResearchProjectDef.description:
Mana is only worth what the colony can put it to. This is the branch that takes the reserve and applies it somewhere: a relay tower carries the network outward so devices far from the pool still count as connected, and the converter line turns stored mana into ordinary electric power for machines that were never built to drink anything else.

A relay stores nothing of its own - a tower whose circle touches no pool-backed node is dead weight and says so on inspection - and a converter runs only while it can find mana to draw. Between them they are what lets a mana economy stand in for a power grid instead of running beside it: fixed points keep working with no fuel, no pawn and no conduit.

Full numbers and derivations: gameplay guide.

ResearchProjectDef.label: mana furniture
ResearchProjectDef.description:
Not every mana device is industrial. A mana lamp is a quartz globe that drinks mana instead of power: light banked in the glass burns there on its own, the lamp draws 1 mana from the network every 60 seconds, and when the supply runs dry the glow dies and the room goes dark until mana returns.

It is the cheapest way to light a base that has no power line, and the first piece of furniture the colony builds out of mana rather than wood and steel - soft, permanent and quiet, with no fuel to haul and no switch a pawn has to flip.

Full numbers and derivations: gameplay guide.

ResearchProjectDef.label: mana repairer
ResearchProjectDef.description:
A mana repairer is not a flower but the rule behind two repair devices: a tower that mends built structures and a bench that mends worn gear. Both settle once every 60 ticks (one second), take the most damaged valid targets first, and pay 5 mana for every point of hit points they put back.

The bill scales with the work: 5 hp costs 25 mana, and a device restoring 5 hp per second on each of five targets draws 125 mana per second. If the network covers only part of the bill the device repairs only what it can pay for, and with no mana it does nothing that second. Bottom line: hp restored x 5 mana = the bill, settled every 60 ticks; no free repairs, and neither device can finish construction or mend a blueprint or frame.

Full numbers and derivations: gameplay guide.

ResearchProjectDef.label: wands
ResearchProjectDef.description: Reforge the wand of the forest into two specialised forms. The sniper form trades rate of fire for one dense lance that punches through armour. The blast form throws slow, unstable bolts that burst into a cross of fire wherever they land, friend or foe. Neither form keeps the wand's plant-magic.

ResearchProjectDef.label: elven
ResearchProjectDef.description:
Elven craft is the tier above manasteel, and it is not forged - it is traded. Raise a gate of livingwood and livingrock with its lintel and both pillars standing, leave livingwood, livingrock or petals in the doorway, and it draws mana from a nearby pool to turn them into dreamwood, elven quartz, pixie dust and elementium ingot.

Elementium is the pink metal that comes out of it: it bends instead of shattering and keeps an edge that steel loses after a single fight, which is why the gear forged from it - a sword, a full suit of plate and a matching helm - sits between manasteel and terrasteel. Nothing the colony can make on its own reaches this shelf; short of what the gaia spirit teaches, this is the top.

Full numbers and derivations: gameplay guide.

ResearchProjectDef.label: terrasteel
ResearchProjectDef.description: Feed manasteel and elven quartz to a ring of four pedestals and draw twenty thousand mana through it. What comes out is terrasteel: metal that grows. Every piece of it buys one blade, one suit of plate or one helm.

ResearchProjectDef.description: Placeholder: unlocked by a gaia spirit techprint, not by points alone. Content arrives in a later version.
